![](images/thomas-baynum.jpg){.headshot fig-alt="Thomas Baynum, smiling, in a navy striped polo shirt against a plain wall."}

Every job I've had came down to making the numbers agree. Route logs and hours of service rules as a CDL Class A driver. Nightly cash and card batches as a restaurant assistant general manager. An average of 800 or more invoices a month as an accountant at a state agency. Now I handle payroll deductions and benefit premiums on a benefits team, and between pay cycles I've built Power BI and Power Query tools that do the matching and show exactly where a variance came from.

I like to know how a system works: when the cash arrives, when a change is keyed, when it posts and when each report runs. Most "errors" turn out to be timing.

I'm open to **data analyst**, **data management** and **AI operations and enablement** roles, and I'm building toward **analytics engineering** and **data engineering** *(see [Where I'm headed](#headed))*: anywhere reconciliation, reporting, clean data and the careful use of AI matter.

## Where it started

There was no set process for pulling a year of payroll data together for 401(k) testing. Then I discovered Power Query, and realized it would work if every pay period's file matched: same tables, same sheet names, clean data. So I made them match, then appended and pivoted a full year into one table.

## Where I'm headed {#headed}

Reconciliation taught me that many bad numbers start upstream, before anyone opens a report. So I'm learning to build the upstream part myself. First comes clean, tested data *(data management)*. Then come models that carry their checks with them *(analytics engineering)*, and then the pipelines that move the data *(data engineering)*. I'm doing it in public, on invented data, in my [Total Rewards analytics platform](projects/total-rewards-platform.qmd).

- GitHub Foundations *(GH-900)*: in progress
- PL-300 Power BI Data Analyst: in progress *([my Power BI work so far, AI-assisted](projects/benefits-ledger.qmd))*
- AWS Cloud Practitioner: planned
- dbt Analytics Engineering: planned
- DP-600 Fabric Analytics Engineer: optional, planned
